question: Why can the best-selling singer earn a thousand times more than one who is only slightly less good?
answer: Because one performance can be copied to millions at almost no extra cost. Sherwin Rosen showed in 1981 that when a recording or broadcast can reach everyone, buyers all pick the best, and the second best gets few sales, not slightly fewer. Small gaps in talent become huge gaps in pay once the work scales.
move: Where work can be copied endlessly, small leads become vast gaps.
ask: Does my work reach more people when I improve it, or is it capped at one client at a time?
reference: Rosen, The Economics of Superstars, American Economic Review, 1981
